When saving your pet comes with guilt: The reality of starvation in Gaza
item.description:
When saving your pet comes with guilt: The reality of starvation in Gaza

In the latest episode of The Gaza Podcast, Palestinian journalist and human rights defender Maha Hussaini introduces her cat Tom, a fellow genocide survivor.

"He couldn’t understand the starvation, the occupation, the blockade or the genocide," Hussaini said. 

Having moved from one shelter to another throughout the war, Tom suffered an eye injury from a soot-covered pot and saw his weight drop in half during the peak of starvation in Gaza.

Maha shares the emotional reality of trying to keep a pet alive when food was nearly impossible to find, and how pets across Gaza continue to suffer as Israel continues to block the entry of essential veterinary supplies.

Trump suggests US may launch further attacks against Iran
item.description:
Trump suggests US may launch further attacks against Iran

US president Donald Trump suggested that Washington may launch more attacks targeting Iran. 

"This should have been done a long time ago by other presidents, the Iran war, and we’ve knocked the hell out of them, and we may do it a little bit further," he told reporters. 

In response to questions about the public reaction to the war on Ira, the US president said: "Well, in one way they love it because I’m doing what should have been done by other presidents. In another way, maybe they don’t."

"There’s a price to pay, which I knew immediately when I did it. But we can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

item.title: Saudi strike on house in Taiz kills, wounds five
item.description:
Saudi strike on house in Taiz kills, wounds five

Saudi strikes on a residential home in the Taiz governorate killed and injured five civilians overnight. 

According to the spokesperson for the Ministry of Health and Environment, one citizen was killed as a result of the attacks and four other were wounded, some in critical condition.

item.title: Watch: Palestinian killed in Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza City
item.description:
Watch: Palestinian killed in Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza City

An Israeli air strike on a vehicle in Gaza City’s Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood killed at least one Palestinian and wounded others.

Another Israeli strike killed one Palestinian in Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, a source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera.

Israeli forces also shot and killed a teenage girl in the al-Faluja area of northern Gaza, shooting her in the head.

Israeli attacks kill 4 Palestinians, including girl, in Gaza amid ceasefire violations
item.description: Israeli strikes and gunfire across the Gaza Strip killed four Palestinians, including a girl, and injured more than 19 others on Thursday amid continued violations of an effective ceasefire agreement, medics said. In the latest attack, a Palestinian was killed when an Israeli drone struck an electric bicycle west of the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip, a medical source said. Another Palestinian was killed and others were injured, one seriously, when an Israeli drone struck a civilian vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood southwest of Gaza City, the source said. item.title: Lebanese president warns regional tensions could spiral into wider escalation
item.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned Thursday that the region faces “very significant” challenges, expressing hope they would not lead to escalation or an “explosion,” Anadolu reports. Aoun made the warning while chairing a Cabinet session at the presidential palace in Baabda, east of Beirut, attended by Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, according to a statement from the Lebanese presidency. “The challenges facing the region are very significant, and I hope their course will not lead toward escalation or explosion,” Aoun said. He urged parties in Lebanon to “exercise wisdom, awareness and restraint” to shield the country from the impact of regional developments, noting that Lebanon is already suffering from difficult economic conditions. “This requires everyone, ministers and political officials, to act wisely […]

item.title: Qatar, US discuss regional de-escalation, maritime navigation
item.description: Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani discussed regional developments and efforts to reduce tensions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a phone call Thursday, according to Qatar’s Foreign Ministry, Anadolu reports. In a statement, the ministry said the two officials reviewed bilateral relations and ways to strengthen the strategic partnership between Qatar and the US. The discussions also addressed the latest regional developments, particularly ongoing diplomatic efforts and joint coordination to de-escalate tensions and enhance regional security and stability. item.title: Indian, Israeli premiers discuss Mideast situation, bilateral ties over phone
item.description: In a Thursday phone call, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu discussed bilateral ties and the situation in the Middle East, Anadolu reports. “The two leaders welcomed the sustained momentum in India-Israel relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the Special Strategic Partnership between the two countries,” said a statement by Modi’s office. New Delhi said the leaders also “exchanged views on recent developments” in the Middle East and “underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region. “ Modi reiterated India’s “call for dialogue and diplomacy as the way forward,” the statement said.
